svg.aria-label: A timeline: Eve records encrypted traffic today and decrypts it once a quantum computer exists, unless a post-quantum key exchange was used
svg.text: the year a big quantum computer works

g.text: …and so the AES key, and so
Unless the key exchange was already post-quantum: then there’s nothing in the recording
that a quantum computer can turn into the key. The protection has to be in place before the recording is made.

ol.li: Today: Eve can’t read Bob’s encrypted traffic (Chapter 31). But disks are cheap, so she records it anyway.
One day, perhaps, a large quantum computer works. It can solve the maths problem behind X25519 (and RSA, and every elliptic curve): from the public keys in the recording, it finds a private one.
With it, Eve redoes the key exchange, runs the same key schedule as Chapter 32, and decrypts the whole conversation. Years late, but for some secrets that doesn’t matter.
That’s why the switch has to happen long before anyone has such a computer.

figure.figcaption: “Harvest now, decrypt later”. The danger for today’s secrets isn’t today’s computers.
